For example, use 'function|method|procedure' to look for all of those words at once. Use includePattern to search within files matching a specific pattern, or in a specific file, using a relative path. Use 'includeIgnoredFiles' to include files normally ignored by .gitignore, other ignore files, and `files.exclude` and `search.exclude` settings. Warning: using this may cause the search to be slower, only set it when you want to search in ignored folders like node_modules or build outputs. Use this tool when you want to see an overview of a particular file, instead of using read_file many times to look for code within a file.

--- MESSAGE 18628 ---
run_in_terminal

--- MESSAGE 18629 ---
This tool allows you to execute shell commands in a persistent bash terminal session, preserving environment variables, working directory, and other context across multiple commands.

Command Execution:
- Use && to chain simple commands on one line
- Prefer pipelines | over temporary files for data flow
- Never create a sub-shell (eg. bash -c "command") unless explicitly asked

Directory Management:
- Must use absolute paths to avoid navigation issues
- Use $PWD for current directory references
- Consider using pushd/popd for directory stack management
- Supports directory shortcuts like ~ and -

Program Execution:
- Supports Python, Node.js, and other executables
- Install packages via package managers (brew, apt, etc.)
- Use which or command -v to verify command availability

Background Processes:
- For long-running tasks (e.g., servers), set isBackground=true
- Returns a terminal ID for checking status and runtime later

Output Management:
- Output is automatically truncated if longer than 60KB to prevent context overflow
- Use head, tail, grep, awk to filter and limit output size
- For pager commands, disable paging: git --no-pager or add | cat
- Use wc -l to count lines before displaying large outputs

Best Practices:
- Quote variables: "$var" instead of $var to handle spaces
- Use find with -exec or xargs for file operations
- Be specific with commands to avoid excessive output
- Avoid printing credentials unless absolutely required
- Use [[ ]] for conditional tests instead of [ ]
- Prefer $() over backticks for command substitution
- Use set -e at start of complex commands to exit on errors

--- MESSAGE 18630 ---
object

--- MESSAGE 18631 ---
string

--- MESSAGE 18632 ---
The command to run in the terminal.

--- MESSAGE 18633 ---
string

--- MESSAGE 18634 ---
A one-sentence description of what the command does. This will be shown to the user before the command is run.

--- MESSAGE 18635 ---
boolean

--- MESSAGE 18636 ---
Whether the command starts a background process. If true, the command will run in the background and you will not see the output. If false, the tool call will block on the command finishing, and then you will get the output. Examples of background processes: building in watch mode, starting a server. You can check the output of a background process later on by using get_terminal_output.

--- MESSAGE 18637 ---
number

--- MESSAGE 18638 ---
An optional timeout in milliseconds. When provided, the tool will stop tracking the command after this duration and return the output collected so far. Be conservative with the timeout duration, give enough time that the command would complete on a low-end machine. Use 0 for no timeout. If it's not clear how long the command will take then use 0 to avoid prematurely terminating it, never guess too low.

--- MESSAGE 18644 ---
runSubagent

--- MESSAGE 18645 ---
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously. This tool is good at researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries, use this agent to perform the search for you.

- Agents do not run async or in the background, you will wait for the agent's result.
- When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.
- Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report. Therefore, your prompt should contain a highly detailed task description for the agent to perform autonomously and you should specify exactly what information the agent should return back to you in its final and only message to you.
- The agent's outputs should generally be trusted
- Clearly tell the agent whether you expect it to write code or just to do research (search, file reads, web fetches, etc.), since it is not aware of the user's intent
- If the user asks for a certain agent, you MUST provide that EXACT agent name (case-sensitive) to invoke that specific agent.

context7_resolve-library-id

--- MESSAGE 18701 ---
Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns a list of matching libraries.

You MUST call this function before 'context7_get-library-docs' to obtain a valid Context7-compatible library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Selection Process:
1. Analyze the query to understand what library/package the user is looking for
2. Return the most relevant match based on:
- Name similarity to the query (exact matches prioritized)
- Description relevance to the query's intent
- Documentation coverage (prioritize libraries with higher Code Snippet counts)
- Trust score (consider libraries with scores of 7-10 more authoritative)

Response Format:
- Return the selected library ID in a clearly marked section
- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen
- If multiple good matches exist, acknowledge this but proceed with the most relevant one
- If no good matches exist, clearly state this and suggest query refinements

For ambiguous queries, request clarification before proceeding with a best-guess match.. Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns a list of matching libraries.

--- MESSAGE 18757 ---
Call this tool when you need access to a new category of tools. The category of tools is described as follows:

This group of tools is designed for managing sub-issues within a parent issue in GitHub repositories. Both tools, 'mcp_github_sub_issue_write' and 'mcp_github2_sub_issue_write', serve the same purpose of adding sub-issues, allowing users to create a hierarchical structure of tasks and discussions related to a main issue. This functionality is particularly useful for teams that need to break down larger tasks into smaller, manageable components, facilitating better organization and tracking of progress. 

By using these tools, developers and project managers can enhance their workflow by ensuring that all related tasks are linked to a parent issue, making it easier to monitor dependencies and relationships between different tasks. This can lead to improved collaboration among team members, as everyone can see how their work contributes to the overall project goals. 

Additionally, the ability to add sub-issues helps in prioritizing tasks, as teams can focus on critical components of a project while keeping track of smaller, related tasks that need to be addressed. This structured approach to issue management can significantly improve project visibility and accountability. 

Overall, these tools are essential for teams utilizing GitHub for project management, as they streamline the process of issue tracking and enhance the clarity of task assignments. By integrating these tools into their workflow, teams can ensure that all aspects of their projects are well-organized and efficiently managed.

Be sure to call this tool if you need a capability related to the above.

mcp_github_pull_request_review_write

--- MESSAGE 18760 ---
Create and/or submit, delete review of a pull request.

Available methods:
- create: Create a new review of a pull request. If "event" parameter is provided, the review is submitted. If "event" is omitted, a pending review is created.
- submit_pending: Submit an existing pending review of a pull request. This requires that a pending review exists for the current user on the specified pull request. The "body" and "event" parameters are used when submitting the review.
- delete_pending: Delete an existing pending review of a pull request. This requires that a pending review exists for the current user on the specified pull request.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
MOE_CYCLE PROOF-GATE - Validates mutation clusters before checkpoint
"""
import subprocess
import sys
import json
from pathlib import Path

def log(stage, status, data):
    print(json.dumps({"stage": stage, "status": status, "data": data}), flush=True)

def run_cmd(cmd, desc):
    """Run command and return success status"""
    log("PROOF_GATE", "running", {"cmd": cmd, "desc": desc})
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
    success = result.returncode == 0
    log("PROOF_GATE", "completed" if success else "failed", {
        "cmd": cmd,
        "exit_code": result.returncode,
        "stdout": result.stdout[:200],
        "stderr": result.stderr[:200]
    })
    return success

def main():
    project_root = Path(__file__).parent
    log("PROOF_GATE", "init", {"root": str(project_root)})
    
    checks = [
        ("python3 scripts/dedi_agent.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Agent syntax check"),
        ("python3 scripts/main.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Main entrypoint syntax"),
        ("python3 -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(\"docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml\"))'", "Compose YAML validity"),
        ("grep -q 'MUTATION_CLUSTER' docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml || true", "MOE cycle marker"),
    ]
    
    passed = 0
    failed = 0
    
    for cmd, desc in checks:
        if run_cmd(cmd, desc):
            passed += 1
        else:
            failed += 1
    
    log("PROOF_GATE", "summary", {"passed": passed, "failed": failed, "total": len(checks)})
    
    if failed > 0:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "REJECT", {"reason": f"{failed} checks failed"})
        sys.exit(1)
    else:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "APPROVE", {"reason": "All checks passed"})
        sys.exit(0)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

--- MESSAGE 19217 ---
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
MOE_CYCLE PROOF-GATE - Validates mutation clusters before checkpoint
"""
import subprocess
import sys
import json
from pathlib import Path

def log(stage, status, data):
    print(json.dumps({"stage": stage, "status": status, "data": data}), flush=True)

def run_cmd(cmd, desc):
    """Run command and return success status"""
    log("PROOF_GATE", "running", {"cmd": cmd, "desc": desc})
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
    success = result.returncode == 0
    log("PROOF_GATE", "completed" if success else "failed", {
        "cmd": cmd,
        "exit_code": result.returncode,
        "stdout": result.stdout[:200],
        "stderr": result.stderr[:200]
    })
    return success

def main():
    project_root = Path(__file__).parent
    log("PROOF_GATE", "init", {"root": str(project_root)})
    
    checks = [
        ("python3 scripts/dedi_agent.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Agent syntax check"),
        ("python3 scripts/main.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Main entrypoint syntax"),
        ("python3 -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(\"docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml\"))'", "Compose YAML validity"),
        ("grep -q 'MUTATION_CLUSTER' docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml || true", "MOE cycle marker"),
    ]
    
    passed = 0
    failed = 0
    
    for cmd, desc in checks:
        if run_cmd(cmd, desc):
            passed += 1
        else:
            failed += 1
    
    log("PROOF_GATE", "summary", {"passed": passed, "failed": failed, "total": len(checks)})
    
    if failed > 0:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "REJECT", {"reason": f"{failed} checks failed"})
        sys.exit(1)
    else:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "APPROVE", {"reason": "All checks passed"})
        sys.exit(0)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
MOE_CYCLE PROOF-GATE - Validates mutation clusters before checkpoint
"""
import subprocess
import sys
import json
from pathlib import Path

def log(stage, status, data):
    print(json.dumps({"stage": stage, "status": status, "data": data}), flush=True)

def run_cmd(cmd, desc):
    """Run command and return success status"""
    log("PROOF_GATE", "running", {"cmd": cmd, "desc": desc})
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
    success = result.returncode == 0
    log("PROOF_GATE", "completed" if success else "failed", {
        "cmd": cmd,
        "exit_code": result.returncode,
        "stdout": result.stdout[:200],
        "stderr": result.stderr[:200]
    })
    return success

def main():
    project_root = Path(__file__).parent
    log("PROOF_GATE", "init", {"root": str(project_root)})
    
    checks = [
        ("python3 scripts/dedi_agent.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Agent syntax check"),
        ("python3 scripts/main.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Main entrypoint syntax"),
        ("python3 -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(\"docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml\"))'", "Compose YAML validity"),
        ("grep -q 'MUTATION_CLUSTER' docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml || true", "MOE cycle marker"),
    ]
    
    passed = 0
    failed = 0
    
    for cmd, desc in checks:
        if run_cmd(cmd, desc):
            passed += 1
        else:
            failed += 1
    
    log("PROOF_GATE", "summary", {"passed": passed, "failed": failed, "total": len(checks)})
    
    if failed > 0:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "REJECT", {"reason": f"{failed} checks failed"})
        sys.exit(1)
    else:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "APPROVE", {"reason": "All checks passed"})
        sys.exit(0)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

--- MESSAGE 19552 ---
apply_patch

--- MESSAGE 19553 ---
Use the `apply_patch` tool to edit files.
Your patch language is a stripped-down, file-oriented diff format designed to be easy to parse and safe to apply. You can think of it as a high-level envelope:

*** Begin Patch
[ one or more file sections ]
*** End Patch

Within that envelope, you get a sequence of file operations.
You MUST include a header to specify the action you are taking.
Each operation starts with one of three headers:

*** Add File: <path> - create a new file. Every following line is a + line (the initial contents).
*** Delete File: <path> - remove an existing file. Nothing follows.
*** Update File: <path> - patch an existing file in place (optionally with a rename).

May be immediately followed by *** Move to: <new path> if you want to rename the file.
Then one or more “hunks”, each introduced by @@ (optionally followed by a hunk header).
Within a hunk each line starts with:

For instructions on [context_before] and [context_after]:
- By default, show 3 lines of code immediately above and 3 lines immediately below each change. If a change is within 3 lines of a previous change, do NOT duplicate the first change's [context_after] lines in the second change's [context_before] lines.
- If 3 lines of context is insufficient to uniquely identify the snippet of code within the file, use the @@ operator to indicate the class or function to which the snippet belongs. For instance, we might have:
@@ class BaseClass
[3 lines of pre-context]
- [old_code]
+ [new_code]
[3 lines of post-context]

- If a code block is repeated so many times in a class or function such that even a single `@@` statement and 3 lines of context cannot uniquely identify the snippet of code, you can use multiple `@@` statements to jump to the right context. For instance:

@@ class BaseClass
@@ 	 def method():
[3 lines of pre-context]
- [old_code]
+ [new_code]
[3 lines of post-context]

The full grammar definition is below:
Patch := Begin { FileOp } End
Begin := "*** Begin Patch" NEWLINE
End := "*** End Patch" NEWLINE
FileOp := AddFile | DeleteFile | UpdateFile
AddFile := "*** Add File: " path NEWLINE { "+" line NEWLINE }
DeleteFile := "*** Delete File: " path NEWLINE
UpdateFile := "*** Update File: " path NEWLINE [ MoveTo ] { Hunk }
MoveTo := "*** Move to: " newPath NEWLINE
Hunk := "@@" [ header ] NEWLINE { HunkLine } [ "*** End of File" NEWLINE ]
HunkLine := (" " | "-" | "+") text NEWLINE

A full patch can combine several operations:

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: hello.txt
+Hello world
*** Update File: src/app.py
*** Move to: src/main.py
@@ def greet():
-print("Hi")
+print("Hello, world!")
*** Delete File: obsolete.txt
*** End Patch

It is important to remember:

- You must include a header with your intended action (Add/Delete/Update)
- You must prefix new lines with `+` even when creating a new file
- File references must be ABSOLUTE, NEVER RELATIVE.

Manage persistent memory across conversations. This tool allows you to create, view, update, and delete memory files that persist between chat sessions. Use this to remember important information about the user, their preferences, project context, or anything that should be recalled in future conversations. Available commands: view (list/read memories), create (new memory file), str_replace (edit content), insert (add content), delete (remove memory), rename (change filename).

--- MESSAGE 19695 ---
run_in_terminal

--- MESSAGE 19696 ---
This tool allows you to execute shell commands in a persistent bash terminal session, preserving environment variables, working directory, and other context across multiple commands.

Command Execution:
- Use && to chain simple commands on one line
- Prefer pipelines | over temporary files for data flow
- Never create a sub-shell (eg. bash -c "command") unless explicitly asked

Directory Management:
- Must use absolute paths to avoid navigation issues
- Use $PWD for current directory references
- Consider using pushd/popd for directory stack management
- Supports directory shortcuts like ~ and -

Program Execution:
- Supports Python, Node.js, and other executables
- Install packages via package managers (brew, apt, etc.)
- Use which or command -v to verify command availability

Background Processes:
- For long-running tasks (e.g., servers), set isBackground=true
- Returns a terminal ID for checking status and runtime later

Output Management:
- Output is automatically truncated if longer than 60KB to prevent context overflow
- Use head, tail, grep, awk to filter and limit output size
- For pager commands, disable paging: git --no-pager or add | cat
- Use wc -l to count lines before displaying large outputs

Best Practices:
- Quote variables: "$var" instead of $var to handle spaces
- Use find with -exec or xargs for file operations
- Be specific with commands to avoid excessive output
- Avoid printing credentials unless absolutely required
- Use [[ ]] for conditional tests instead of [ ]
- Prefer $() over backticks for command substitution
- Use set -e at start of complex commands to exit on errors

--- MESSAGE 19697 ---
object

--- MESSAGE 19698 ---
string

--- MESSAGE 19699 ---
The command to run in the terminal.

--- MESSAGE 19700 ---
string

--- MESSAGE 19701 ---
A one-sentence description of what the command does. This will be shown to the user before the command is run.

--- MESSAGE 19702 ---
boolean

--- MESSAGE 19703 ---
Whether the command starts a background process. If true, the command will run in the background and you will not see the output. If false, the tool call will block on the command finishing, and then you will get the output. Examples of background processes: building in watch mode, starting a server. You can check the output of a background process later on by using get_terminal_output.

--- MESSAGE 19704 ---
number

--- MESSAGE 19705 ---
An optional timeout in milliseconds. When provided, the tool will stop tracking the command after this duration and return the output collected so far. Be conservative with the timeout duration, give enough time that the command would complete on a low-end machine. Use 0 for no timeout. If it's not clear how long the command will take then use 0 to avoid prematurely terminating it, never guess too low.

--- MESSAGE 19711 ---
runSubagent

--- MESSAGE 19712 ---
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously. This tool is good at researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries, use this agent to perform the search for you.

- Agents do not run async or in the background, you will wait for the agent's result.
- When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.
- Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report. Therefore, your prompt should contain a highly detailed task description for the agent to perform autonomously and you should specify exactly what information the agent should return back to you in its final and only message to you.
- The agent's outputs should generally be trusted
- Clearly tell the agent whether you expect it to write code or just to do research (search, file reads, web fetches, etc.), since it is not aware of the user's intent
- If the user asks for a certain agent, you MUST provide that EXACT agent name (case-sensitive) to invoke that specific agent.

Optional name of a specific agent to invoke. If not provided, uses the current agent.

context7_resolve-library-id

--- MESSAGE 19768 ---
Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns a list of matching libraries.

You MUST call this function before 'context7_get-library-docs' to obtain a valid Context7-compatible library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Selection Process:
1. Analyze the query to understand what library/package the user is looking for
2. Return the most relevant match based on:
- Name similarity to the query (exact matches prioritized)
- Description relevance to the query's intent
- Documentation coverage (prioritize libraries with higher Code Snippet counts)
- Trust score (consider libraries with scores of 7-10 more authoritative)

Response Format:
- Return the selected library ID in a clearly marked section
- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen
- If multiple good matches exist, acknowledge this but proceed with the most relevant one
- If no good matches exist, clearly state this and suggest query refinements

For ambiguous queries, request clarification before proceeding with a best-guess match.. Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns a list of matching libraries.

--- MESSAGE 19826 ---
mcp_github_pull_request_review_write

--- MESSAGE 19827 ---
Create and/or submit, delete review of a pull request.

Available methods:
- create: Create a new review of a pull request. If "event" parameter is provided, the review is submitted. If "event" is omitted, a pending review is created.
- submit_pending: Submit an existing pending review of a pull request. This requires that a pending review exists for the current user on the specified pull request. The "body" and "event" parameters are used when submitting the review.
- delete_pending: Delete an existing pending review of a pull request. This requires that a pending review exists for the current user on the specified pull request.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
MOE_CYCLE PROOF-GATE - Validates mutation clusters before checkpoint
"""
import subprocess
import sys
import json
from pathlib import Path

def log(stage, status, data):
    print(json.dumps({"stage": stage, "status": status, "data": data}), flush=True)

def run_cmd(cmd, desc):
    """Run command and return success status"""
    log("PROOF_GATE", "running", {"cmd": cmd, "desc": desc})
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
    success = result.returncode == 0
    log("PROOF_GATE", "completed" if success else "failed", {
        "cmd": cmd,
        "exit_code": result.returncode,
        "stdout": result.stdout[:200],
        "stderr": result.stderr[:200]
    })
    return success

def main():
    project_root = Path(__file__).parent
    log("PROOF_GATE", "init", {"root": str(project_root)})
    
    checks = [
        ("python3 scripts/dedi_agent.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Agent syntax check"),
        ("python3 scripts/main.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Main entrypoint syntax"),
        ("python3 -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(\"docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml\"))'", "Compose YAML validity"),
        ("grep -q 'MUTATION_CLUSTER' docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml || true", "MOE cycle marker"),
    ]
    
    passed = 0
    failed = 0
    
    for cmd, desc in checks:
        if run_cmd(cmd, desc):
            passed += 1
        else:
            failed += 1
    
    log("PROOF_GATE", "summary", {"passed": passed, "failed": failed, "total": len(checks)})
    
    if failed > 0:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "REJECT", {"reason": f"{failed} checks failed"})
        sys.exit(1)
    else:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "APPROVE", {"reason": "All checks passed"})
        sys.exit(0)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

--- MESSAGE 20284 ---
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
MOE_CYCLE PROOF-GATE - Validates mutation clusters before checkpoint
"""
import subprocess
import sys
import json
from pathlib import Path

def log(stage, status, data):
    print(json.dumps({"stage": stage, "status": status, "data": data}), flush=True)

def run_cmd(cmd, desc):
    """Run command and return success status"""
    log("PROOF_GATE", "running", {"cmd": cmd, "desc": desc})
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
    success = result.returncode == 0
    log("PROOF_GATE", "completed" if success else "failed", {
        "cmd": cmd,
        "exit_code": result.returncode,
        "stdout": result.stdout[:200],
        "stderr": result.stderr[:200]
    })
    return success

def main():
    project_root = Path(__file__).parent
    log("PROOF_GATE", "init", {"root": str(project_root)})
    
    checks = [
        ("python3 scripts/dedi_agent.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Agent syntax check"),
        ("python3 scripts/main.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Main entrypoint syntax"),
        ("python3 -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(\"docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml\"))'", "Compose YAML validity"),
        ("grep -q 'MUTATION_CLUSTER' docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml || true", "MOE cycle marker"),
    ]
    
    passed = 0
    failed = 0
    
    for cmd, desc in checks:
        if run_cmd(cmd, desc):
            passed += 1
        else:
            failed += 1
    
    log("PROOF_GATE", "summary", {"passed": passed, "failed": failed, "total": len(checks)})
    
    if failed > 0:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "REJECT", {"reason": f"{failed} checks failed"})
        sys.exit(1)
    else:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "APPROVE", {"reason": "All checks passed"})
        sys.exit(0)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

--- MESSAGE 20532 ---
Done. I added VS Code shell integration sourcing and tightened the timeout logic so we don’t nuke builds:

- **VS Code integration**: The wrapper now sources the VS Code shell integration script if `VSCODE_SHELL_INTEGRATION` is provided (or the default vscode-server path when `TERM_PROGRAM=vscode`). Logging notes which file was sourced.
- **Timeouts made safer**:
  - Defaults: `AIS_SHELL_TIMEOUT_ENABLED=true`, `AIS_SHELL_TIMEOUT=5`.
  - **Whitelist** for long builds/tools (no timeout if the command matches): `make|cmake|ninja|npm|yarn|pnpm|bun|uv|pip|poetry|docker build|docker-compose|kubectl|helm|gradle|mvn|cargo`.

--- MESSAGE 20630 ---
apply_patch

--- MESSAGE 20631 ---
Use the `apply_patch` tool to edit files.
Your patch language is a stripped-down, file-oriented diff format designed to be easy to parse and safe to apply. You can think of it as a high-level envelope:

*** Begin Patch
[ one or more file sections ]
*** End Patch

Within that envelope, you get a sequence of file operations.
You MUST include a header to specify the action you are taking.
Each operation starts with one of three headers:

*** Add File: <path> - create a new file. Every following line is a + line (the initial contents).
*** Delete File: <path> - remove an existing file. Nothing follows.
*** Update File: <path> - patch an existing file in place (optionally with a rename).

May be immediately followed by *** Move to: <new path> if you want to rename the file.
Then one or more “hunks”, each introduced by @@ (optionally followed by a hunk header).
Within a hunk each line starts with:

For instructions on [context_before] and [context_after]:
- By default, show 3 lines of code immediately above and 3 lines immediately below each change. If a change is within 3 lines of a previous change, do NOT duplicate the first change's [context_after] lines in the second change's [context_before] lines.
- If 3 lines of context is insufficient to uniquely identify the snippet of code within the file, use the @@ operator to indicate the class or function to which the snippet belongs. For instance, we might have:
@@ class BaseClass
[3 lines of pre-context]
- [old_code]
+ [new_code]
[3 lines of post-context]

- If a code block is repeated so many times in a class or function such that even a single `@@` statement and 3 lines of context cannot uniquely identify the snippet of code, you can use multiple `@@` statements to jump to the right context. For instance:

@@ class BaseClass
@@ 	 def method():
[3 lines of pre-context]
- [old_code]
+ [new_code]
[3 lines of post-context]

The full grammar definition is below:
Patch := Begin { FileOp } End
Begin := "*** Begin Patch" NEWLINE
End := "*** End Patch" NEWLINE
FileOp := AddFile | DeleteFile | UpdateFile
AddFile := "*** Add File: " path NEWLINE { "+" line NEWLINE }
DeleteFile := "*** Delete File: " path NEWLINE
UpdateFile := "*** Update File: " path NEWLINE [ MoveTo ] { Hunk }
MoveTo := "*** Move to: " newPath NEWLINE
Hunk := "@@" [ header ] NEWLINE { HunkLine } [ "*** End of File" NEWLINE ]
HunkLine := (" " | "-" | "+") text NEWLINE

A full patch can combine several operations:

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: hello.txt
+Hello world
*** Update File: src/app.py
*** Move to: src/main.py
@@ def greet():
-print("Hi")
+print("Hello, world!")
*** Delete File: obsolete.txt
*** End Patch

It is important to remember:

- You must include a header with your intended action (Add/Delete/Update)
- You must prefix new lines with `+` even when creating a new file
- File references must be ABSOLUTE, NEVER RELATIVE.

--- MESSAGE 20773 ---
run_in_terminal

--- MESSAGE 20774 ---
This tool allows you to execute shell commands in a persistent bash terminal session, preserving environment variables, working directory, and other context across multiple commands.

Command Execution:
- Use && to chain simple commands on one line
- Prefer pipelines | over temporary files for data flow
- Never create a sub-shell (eg. bash -c "command") unless explicitly asked

Directory Management:
- Must use absolute paths to avoid navigation issues
- Use $PWD for current directory references
- Consider using pushd/popd for directory stack management
- Supports directory shortcuts like ~ and -

Program Execution:
- Supports Python, Node.js, and other executables
- Install packages via package managers (brew, apt, etc.)
- Use which or command -v to verify command availability

Background Processes:
- For long-running tasks (e.g., servers), set isBackground=true
- Returns a terminal ID for checking status and runtime later

Output Management:
- Output is automatically truncated if longer than 60KB to prevent context overflow
- Use head, tail, grep, awk to filter and limit output size
- For pager commands, disable paging: git --no-pager or add | cat
- Use wc -l to count lines before displaying large outputs

Best Practices:
- Quote variables: "$var" instead of $var to handle spaces
- Use find with -exec or xargs for file operations
- Be specific with commands to avoid excessive output
- Avoid printing credentials unless absolutely required
- Use [[ ]] for conditional tests instead of [ ]
- Prefer $() over backticks for command substitution
- Use set -e at start of complex commands to exit on errors

--- MESSAGE 20775 ---
object

--- MESSAGE 20776 ---
string

--- MESSAGE 20777 ---
The command to run in the terminal.

--- MESSAGE 20778 ---
string

--- MESSAGE 20779 ---
A one-sentence description of what the command does. This will be shown to the user before the command is run.

--- MESSAGE 20780 ---
boolean

--- MESSAGE 20781 ---
Whether the command starts a background process. If true, the command will run in the background and you will not see the output. If false, the tool call will block on the command finishing, and then you will get the output. Examples of background processes: building in watch mode, starting a server. You can check the output of a background process later on by using get_terminal_output.

--- MESSAGE 20782 ---
number

--- MESSAGE 20783 ---
An optional timeout in milliseconds. When provided, the tool will stop tracking the command after this duration and return the output collected so far. Be conservative with the timeout duration, give enough time that the command would complete on a low-end machine. Use 0 for no timeout. If it's not clear how long the command will take then use 0 to avoid prematurely terminating it, never guess too low.

--- MESSAGE 20789 ---
runSubagent

--- MESSAGE 20790 ---
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously. This tool is good at researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries, use this agent to perform the search for you.

- Agents do not run async or in the background, you will wait for the agent's result.
- When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.
- Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report. Therefore, your prompt should contain a highly detailed task description for the agent to perform autonomously and you should specify exactly what information the agent should return back to you in its final and only message to you.
- The agent's outputs should generally be trusted
- Clearly tell the agent whether you expect it to write code or just to do research (search, file reads, web fetches, etc.), since it is not aware of the user's intent
- If the user asks for a certain agent, you MUST provide that EXACT agent name (case-sensitive) to invoke that specific agent.

context7_resolve-library-id

--- MESSAGE 20846 ---
Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns a list of matching libraries.

You MUST call this function before 'context7_get-library-docs' to obtain a valid Context7-compatible library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Selection Process:
1. Analyze the query to understand what library/package the user is looking for
2. Return the most relevant match based on:
- Name similarity to the query (exact matches prioritized)
- Description relevance to the query's intent
- Documentation coverage (prioritize libraries with higher Code Snippet counts)
- Trust score (consider libraries with scores of 7-10 more authoritative)

Response Format:
- Return the selected library ID in a clearly marked section
- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen
- If multiple good matches exist, acknowledge this but proceed with the most relevant one
- If no good matches exist, clearly state this and suggest query refinements

For ambiguous queries, request clarification before proceeding with a best-guess match.. Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns a list of matching libraries.

You MUST call this function before 'get-library-docs' to obtain a valid Context7-compatible library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

--- MESSAGE 20904 ---
mcp_github_pull_request_review_write

--- MESSAGE 20905 ---
Create and/or submit, delete review of a pull request.

Available methods:
- create: Create a new review of a pull request. If "event" parameter is provided, the review is submitted. If "event" is omitted, a pending review is created.
- submit_pending: Submit an existing pending review of a pull request. This requires that a pending review exists for the current user on the specified pull request. The "body" and "event" parameters are used when submitting the review.
- delete_pending: Delete an existing pending review of a pull request. This requires that a pending review exists for the current user on the specified pull request.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
MOE_CYCLE PROOF-GATE - Validates mutation clusters before checkpoint
"""
import subprocess
import sys
import json
from pathlib import Path

def log(stage, status, data):
    print(json.dumps({"stage": stage, "status": status, "data": data}), flush=True)

def run_cmd(cmd, desc):
    """Run command and return success status"""
    log("PROOF_GATE", "running", {"cmd": cmd, "desc": desc})
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
    success = result.returncode == 0
    log("PROOF_GATE", "completed" if success else "failed", {
        "cmd": cmd,
        "exit_code": result.returncode,
        "stdout": result.stdout[:200],
        "stderr": result.stderr[:200]
    })
    return success

def main():
    project_root = Path(__file__).parent
    log("PROOF_GATE", "init", {"root": str(project_root)})
    
    checks = [
        ("python3 scripts/dedi_agent.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Agent syntax check"),
        ("python3 scripts/main.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Main entrypoint syntax"),
        ("python3 -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(\"docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml\"))'", "Compose YAML validity"),
        ("grep -q 'MUTATION_CLUSTER' docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml || true", "MOE cycle marker"),
    ]
    
    passed = 0
    failed = 0
    
    for cmd, desc in checks:
        if run_cmd(cmd, desc):
            passed += 1
        else:
            failed += 1
    
    log("PROOF_GATE", "summary", {"passed": passed, "failed": failed, "total": len(checks)})
    
    if failed > 0:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "REJECT", {"reason": f"{failed} checks failed"})
        sys.exit(1)
    else:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "APPROVE", {"reason": "All checks passed"})
        sys.exit(0)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

--- MESSAGE 21362 ---
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
MOE_CYCLE PROOF-GATE - Validates mutation clusters before checkpoint
"""
import subprocess
import sys
import json
from pathlib import Path

def log(stage, status, data):
    print(json.dumps({"stage": stage, "status": status, "data": data}), flush=True)

def run_cmd(cmd, desc):
    """Run command and return success status"""
    log("PROOF_GATE", "running", {"cmd": cmd, "desc": desc})
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
    success = result.returncode == 0
    log("PROOF_GATE", "completed" if success else "failed", {
        "cmd": cmd,
        "exit_code": result.returncode,
        "stdout": result.stdout[:200],
        "stderr": result.stderr[:200]
    })
    return success

def main():
    project_root = Path(__file__).parent
    log("PROOF_GATE", "init", {"root": str(project_root)})
    
    checks = [
        ("python3 scripts/dedi_agent.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Agent syntax check"),
        ("python3 scripts/main.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Main entrypoint syntax"),
        ("python3 -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(\"docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml\"))'", "Compose YAML validity"),
        ("grep -q 'MUTATION_CLUSTER' docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml || true", "MOE cycle marker"),
    ]
    
    passed = 0
    failed = 0
    
    for cmd, desc in checks:
        if run_cmd(cmd, desc):
            passed += 1
        else:
            failed += 1
    
    log("PROOF_GATE", "summary", {"passed": passed, "failed": failed, "total": len(checks)})
    
    if failed > 0:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "REJECT", {"reason": f"{failed} checks failed"})
        sys.exit(1)
    else:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "APPROVE", {"reason": "All checks passed"})
        sys.exit(0)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

--- MESSAGE 21610 ---
Done. I added VS Code shell integration sourcing and tightened the timeout logic so we don’t nuke builds:

- **VS Code integration**: The wrapper now sources the VS Code shell integration script if `VSCODE_SHELL_INTEGRATION` is provided (or the default vscode-server path when `TERM_PROGRAM=vscode`). Logging notes which file was sourced.
- **Timeouts made safer**:
  - Defaults: `AIS_SHELL_TIMEOUT_ENABLED=true`, `AIS_SHELL_TIMEOUT=5`.
  - **Whitelist** for long builds/tools (no timeout if the command matches): `make|cmake|ninja|npm|yarn|pnpm|bun|uv|pip|poetry|docker build|docker-compose|kubectl|helm|gradle|mvn|cargo`.
  - Only our bash children are cleaned up; the aggressive `-9` catch-all was removed to avoid killing unrelated builds.
- Smoke tests:
  - Non-whitelisted (`sleep 6; echo …`) timed out cleanly.
  - Whitelisted (`npm run build && sleep 6`) ran through (npm complained about missing script, but the wrapper didn’t time it out).

Tunable envs:
- `AIS_SHELL_TIMEOUT_ENABLED` (true/false)
- `AIS_SHELL_TIMEOUT` (seconds)
- `AIS_SHELL_TIMEOUT_WHITELIST` (regex fragments, space-separated)
- `AIS_SHELL_DEBUG=true` for debug logs.

Files touched:
- `/home/toxic/antigravity-white/bin/ais_shell_wrapper.sh`

Let me know if you want the timeout default relaxed further or a per-command opt-out flag (e.g., `AIS_SHELL_NO_TIMEOUT=1`).

apply_patch

--- MESSAGE 21720 ---
Use the `apply_patch` tool to edit files.
Your patch language is a stripped-down, file-oriented diff format designed to be easy to parse and safe to apply. You can think of it as a high-level envelope:

*** Begin Patch
[ one or more file sections ]
*** End Patch

Within that envelope, you get a sequence of file operations.
You MUST include a header to specify the action you are taking.
Each operation starts with one of three headers:

*** Add File: <path> - create a new file. Every following line is a + line (the initial contents).
*** Delete File: <path> - remove an existing file. Nothing follows.
*** Update File: <path> - patch an existing file in place (optionally with a rename).

May be immediately followed by *** Move to: <new path> if you want to rename the file.
Then one or more “hunks”, each introduced by @@ (optionally followed by a hunk header).
Within a hunk each line starts with:

For instructions on [context_before] and [context_after]:
- By default, show 3 lines of code immediately above and 3 lines immediately below each change. If a change is within 3 lines of a previous change, do NOT duplicate the first change's [context_after] lines in the second change's [context_before] lines.
- If 3 lines of context is insufficient to uniquely identify the snippet of code within the file, use the @@ operator to indicate the class or function to which the snippet belongs. For instance, we might have:
@@ class BaseClass
[3 lines of pre-context]
- [old_code]
+ [new_code]
[3 lines of post-context]

- If a code block is repeated so many times in a class or function such that even a single `@@` statement and 3 lines of context cannot uniquely identify the snippet of code, you can use multiple `@@` statements to jump to the right context. For instance:

@@ class BaseClass
@@ 	 def method():
[3 lines of pre-context]
- [old_code]
+ [new_code]
[3 lines of post-context]

The full grammar definition is below:
Patch := Begin { FileOp } End
Begin := "*** Begin Patch" NEWLINE
End := "*** End Patch" NEWLINE
FileOp := AddFile | DeleteFile | UpdateFile
AddFile := "*** Add File: " path NEWLINE { "+" line NEWLINE }
DeleteFile := "*** Delete File: " path NEWLINE
UpdateFile := "*** Update File: " path NEWLINE [ MoveTo ] { Hunk }
MoveTo := "*** Move to: " newPath NEWLINE
Hunk := "@@" [ header ] NEWLINE { HunkLine } [ "*** End of File" NEWLINE ]
HunkLine := (" " | "-" | "+") text NEWLINE

A full patch can combine several operations:

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: hello.txt
+Hello world
*** Update File: src/app.py
*** Move to: src/main.py
@@ def greet():
-print("Hi")
+print("Hello, world!")
*** Delete File: obsolete.txt
*** End Patch

It is important to remember:

- You must include a header with your intended action (Add/Delete/Update)
- You must prefix new lines with `+` even when creating a new file
- File references must be ABSOLUTE, NEVER RELATIVE.

--- MESSAGE 21862 ---
run_in_terminal

--- MESSAGE 21863 ---
This tool allows you to execute shell commands in a persistent bash terminal session, preserving environment variables, working directory, and other context across multiple commands.

Command Execution:
- Use && to chain simple commands on one line
- Prefer pipelines | over temporary files for data flow
- Never create a sub-shell (eg. bash -c "command") unless explicitly asked

Directory Management:
- Must use absolute paths to avoid navigation issues
- Use $PWD for current directory references
- Consider using pushd/popd for directory stack management
- Supports directory shortcuts like ~ and -

Program Execution:
- Supports Python, Node.js, and other executables
- Install packages via package managers (brew, apt, etc.)
- Use which or command -v to verify command availability

Background Processes:
- For long-running tasks (e.g., servers), set isBackground=true
- Returns a terminal ID for checking status and runtime later

Output Management:
- Output is automatically truncated if longer than 60KB to prevent context overflow
- Use head, tail, grep, awk to filter and limit output size
- For pager commands, disable paging: git --no-pager or add | cat
- Use wc -l to count lines before displaying large outputs

Best Practices:
- Quote variables: "$var" instead of $var to handle spaces
- Use find with -exec or xargs for file operations
- Be specific with commands to avoid excessive output
- Avoid printing credentials unless absolutely required
- Use [[ ]] for conditional tests instead of [ ]
- Prefer $() over backticks for command substitution
- Use set -e at start of complex commands to exit on errors

--- MESSAGE 21864 ---
object

--- MESSAGE 21865 ---
string

--- MESSAGE 21866 ---
The command to run in the terminal.

--- MESSAGE 21867 ---
string

--- MESSAGE 21868 ---
A one-sentence description of what the command does. This will be shown to the user before the command is run.

--- MESSAGE 21869 ---
boolean

--- MESSAGE 21870 ---
Whether the command starts a background process. If true, the command will run in the background and you will not see the output. If false, the tool call will block on the command finishing, and then you will get the output. Examples of background processes: building in watch mode, starting a server. You can check the output of a background process later on by using get_terminal_output.

--- MESSAGE 21871 ---
number

--- MESSAGE 21872 ---
An optional timeout in milliseconds. When provided, the tool will stop tracking the command after this duration and return the output collected so far. Be conservative with the timeout duration, give enough time that the command would complete on a low-end machine. Use 0 for no timeout. If it's not clear how long the command will take then use 0 to avoid prematurely terminating it, never guess too low.

--- MESSAGE 21878 ---
runSubagent

--- MESSAGE 21879 ---
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously. This tool is good at researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries, use this agent to perform the search for you.

- Agents do not run async or in the background, you will wait for the agent's result.
- When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.
- Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report. Therefore, your prompt should contain a highly detailed task description for the agent to perform autonomously and you should specify exactly what information the agent should return back to you in its final and only message to you.
- The agent's outputs should generally be trusted
- Clearly tell the agent whether you expect it to write code or just to do research (search, file reads, web fetches, etc.), since it is not aware of the user's intent
- If the user asks for a certain agent, you MUST provide that EXACT agent name (case-sensitive) to invoke that specific agent.

context7_resolve-library-id

--- MESSAGE 21935 ---
Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns a list of matching libraries.

You MUST call this function before 'context7_get-library-docs' to obtain a valid Context7-compatible library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Selection Process:
1. Analyze the query to understand what library/package the user is looking for
2. Return the most relevant match based on:
- Name similarity to the query (exact matches prioritized)
- Description relevance to the query's intent
- Documentation coverage (prioritize libraries with higher Code Snippet counts)
- Trust score (consider libraries with scores of 7-10 more authoritative)

Response Format:
- Return the selected library ID in a clearly marked section
- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen
- If multiple good matches exist, acknowledge this but proceed with the most relevant one
- If no good matches exist, clearly state this and suggest query refinements

For ambiguous queries, request clarification before proceeding with a best-guess match.. Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns a list of matching libraries.

mcp_github_pull_request_review_write

--- MESSAGE 21994 ---
Create and/or submit, delete review of a pull request.

Available methods:
- create: Create a new review of a pull request. If "event" parameter is provided, the review is submitted. If "event" is omitted, a pending review is created.
- submit_pending: Submit an existing pending review of a pull request. This requires that a pending review exists for the current user on the specified pull request. The "body" and "event" parameters are used when submitting the review.
- delete_pending: Delete an existing pending review of a pull request. This requires that a pending review exists for the current user on the specified pull request.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
MOE_CYCLE PROOF-GATE - Validates mutation clusters before checkpoint
"""
import subprocess
import sys
import json
from pathlib import Path

def log(stage, status, data):
    print(json.dumps({"stage": stage, "status": status, "data": data}), flush=True)

def run_cmd(cmd, desc):
    """Run command and return success status"""
    log("PROOF_GATE", "running", {"cmd": cmd, "desc": desc})
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
    success = result.returncode == 0
    log("PROOF_GATE", "completed" if success else "failed", {
        "cmd": cmd,
        "exit_code": result.returncode,
        "stdout": result.stdout[:200],
        "stderr": result.stderr[:200]
    })
    return success

def main():
    project_root = Path(__file__).parent
    log("PROOF_GATE", "init", {"root": str(project_root)})
    
    checks = [
        ("python3 scripts/dedi_agent.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Agent syntax check"),
        ("python3 scripts/main.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Main entrypoint syntax"),
        ("python3 -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(\"docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml\"))'", "Compose YAML validity"),
        ("grep -q 'MUTATION_CLUSTER' docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml || true", "MOE cycle marker"),
    ]
    
    passed = 0
    failed = 0
    
    for cmd, desc in checks:
        if run_cmd(cmd, desc):
            passed += 1
        else:
            failed += 1
    
    log("PROOF_GATE", "summary", {"passed": passed, "failed": failed, "total": len(checks)})
    
    if failed > 0:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "REJECT", {"reason": f"{failed} checks failed"})
        sys.exit(1)
    else:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "APPROVE", {"reason": "All checks passed"})
        sys.exit(0)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
MOE_CYCLE PROOF-GATE - Validates mutation clusters before checkpoint
"""
import subprocess
import sys
import json
from pathlib import Path

def log(stage, status, data):
    print(json.dumps({"stage": stage, "status": status, "data": data}), flush=True)

def run_cmd(cmd, desc):
    """Run command and return success status"""
    log("PROOF_GATE", "running", {"cmd": cmd, "desc": desc})
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
    success = result.returncode == 0
    log("PROOF_GATE", "completed" if success else "failed", {
        "cmd": cmd,
        "exit_code": result.returncode,
        "stdout": result.stdout[:200],
        "stderr": result.stderr[:200]
    })
    return success

def main():
    project_root = Path(__file__).parent
    log("PROOF_GATE", "init", {"root": str(project_root)})
    
    checks = [
        ("python3 scripts/dedi_agent.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Agent syntax check"),
        ("python3 scripts/main.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Main entrypoint syntax"),
        ("python3 -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(\"docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml\"))'", "Compose YAML validity"),
        ("grep -q 'MUTATION_CLUSTER' docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml || true", "MOE cycle marker"),
    ]
    
    passed = 0
    failed = 0
    
    for cmd, desc in checks:
        if run_cmd(cmd, desc):
            passed += 1
        else:
            failed += 1
    
    log("PROOF_GATE", "summary", {"passed": passed, "failed": failed, "total": len(checks)})
    
    if failed > 0:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "REJECT", {"reason": f"{failed} checks failed"})
        sys.exit(1)
    else:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "APPROVE", {"reason": "All checks passed"})
        sys.exit(0)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

--- MESSAGE 22699 ---
Done. I added VS Code shell integration sourcing and tightened the timeout logic so we don’t nuke builds:

- **VS Code integration**: The wrapper now sources the VS Code shell integration script if `VSCODE_SHELL_INTEGRATION` is provided (or the default vscode-server path when `TERM_PROGRAM=vscode`). Logging notes which file was sourced.
- **Timeouts made safer**:
  - Defaults: `AIS_SHELL_TIMEOUT_ENABLED=true`, `AIS_SHELL_TIMEOUT=5`.
  - **Whitelist** for long builds/tools (no timeout if the command matches): `make|cmake|ninja|npm|yarn|pnpm|bun|uv|pip|poetry|docker build|docker-compose|kubectl|helm|gradle|mvn|cargo`.

--- MESSAGE 22820 ---
apply_patch

--- MESSAGE 22821 ---
Use the `apply_patch` tool to edit files.
Your patch language is a stripped-down, file-oriented diff format designed to be easy to parse and safe to apply. You can think of it as a high-level envelope:

*** Begin Patch
[ one or more file sections ]
*** End Patch

Within that envelope, you get a sequence of file operations.
You MUST include a header to specify the action you are taking.
Each operation starts with one of three headers:

*** Add File: <path> - create a new file. Every following line is a + line (the initial contents).
*** Delete File: <path> - remove an existing file. Nothing follows.
*** Update File: <path> - patch an existing file in place (optionally with a rename).

May be immediately followed by *** Move to: <new path> if you want to rename the file.
Then one or more “hunks”, each introduced by @@ (optionally followed by a hunk header).
Within a hunk each line starts with:

For instructions on [context_before] and [context_after]:
- By default, show 3 lines of code immediately above and 3 lines immediately below each change. If a change is within 3 lines of a previous change, do NOT duplicate the first change's [context_after] lines in the second change's [context_before] lines.
- If 3 lines of context is insufficient to uniquely identify the snippet of code within the file, use the @@ operator to indicate the class or function to which the snippet belongs. For instance, we might have:
@@ class BaseClass
[3 lines of pre-context]
- [old_code]
+ [new_code]
[3 lines of post-context]

- If a code block is repeated so many times in a class or function such that even a single `@@` statement and 3 lines of context cannot uniquely identify the snippet of code, you can use multiple `@@` statements to jump to the right context. For instance:

@@ class BaseClass
@@ 	 def method():
[3 lines of pre-context]
- [old_code]
+ [new_code]
[3 lines of post-context]

The full grammar definition is below:
Patch := Begin { FileOp } End
Begin := "*** Begin Patch" NEWLINE
End := "*** End Patch" NEWLINE
FileOp := AddFile | DeleteFile | UpdateFile
AddFile := "*** Add File: " path NEWLINE { "+" line NEWLINE }
DeleteFile := "*** Delete File: " path NEWLINE
UpdateFile := "*** Update File: " path NEWLINE [ MoveTo ] { Hunk }
MoveTo := "*** Move to: " newPath NEWLINE
Hunk := "@@" [ header ] NEWLINE { HunkLine } [ "*** End of File" NEWLINE ]
HunkLine := (" " | "-" | "+") text NEWLINE

A full patch can combine several operations:

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: hello.txt
+Hello world

file_search

--- MESSAGE 22848 ---
Search for files in the workspace by glob pattern. This only returns the paths of matching files. Use this tool when you know the exact filename pattern of the files you're searching for. Glob patterns match from the root of the workspace folder. Examples:
- **/*.{js,ts} to match all js/ts files in the workspace.
- src/** to match all files under the top-level src folder.
- **/foo/**/*.js to match all js files under any foo folder in the workspace.

grep_search

--- MESSAGE 22857 ---
Do a fast text search in the workspace. Use this tool when you want to search with an exact string or regex. If you are not sure what words will appear in the workspace, prefer using regex patterns with alternation (|) or character classes to search for multiple potential words at once instead of making separate searches. For example, use 'function|method|procedure' to look for all of those words at once. Use includePattern to search within files matching a specific pattern, or in a specific file, using a relative path. Use 'includeIgnoredFiles' to include files normally ignored by .gitignore, other ignore files, and `files.exclude` and `search.exclude` settings. Warning: using this may cause the search to be slower, only set it when you want to search in ignored folders like node_modules or build outputs. Use this tool when you want to see an overview of a particular file, instead of using read_file many times to look for code within a file.

Be sure to set the isRegexp property properly to declare whether it's a regex or plain text pattern. Is case-insensitive.

--- MESSAGE 22963 ---
run_in_terminal

--- MESSAGE 22964 ---
This tool allows you to execute shell commands in a persistent bash terminal session, preserving environment variables, working directory, and other context across multiple commands.

Command Execution:
- Use && to chain simple commands on one line
- Prefer pipelines | over temporary files for data flow
- Never create a sub-shell (eg. bash -c "command") unless explicitly asked

Directory Management:
- Must use absolute paths to avoid navigation issues
- Use $PWD for current directory references
- Consider using pushd/popd for directory stack management
- Supports directory shortcuts like ~ and -

Program Execution:
- Supports Python, Node.js, and other executables
- Install packages via package managers (brew, apt, etc.)
- Use which or command -v to verify command availability

Background Processes:
- For long-running tasks (e.g., servers), set isBackground=true
- Returns a terminal ID for checking status and runtime later

Output Management:
- Output is automatically truncated if longer than 60KB to prevent context overflow
- Use head, tail, grep, awk to filter and limit output size
- For pager commands, disable paging: git --no-pager or add | cat
- Use wc -l to count lines before displaying large outputs

Best Practices:
- Quote variables: "$var" instead of $var to handle spaces
- Use find with -exec or xargs for file operations
- Be specific with commands to avoid excessive output
- Avoid printing credentials unless absolutely required
- Use [[ ]] for conditional tests instead of [ ]
- Prefer $() over backticks for command substitution
- Use set -e at start of complex commands to exit on errors

--- MESSAGE 22965 ---
object

--- MESSAGE 22966 ---
string

--- MESSAGE 22967 ---
The command to run in the terminal.

--- MESSAGE 22968 ---
string

--- MESSAGE 22969 ---
A one-sentence description of what the command does. This will be shown to the user before the command is run.

--- MESSAGE 22970 ---
boolean

--- MESSAGE 22971 ---
Whether the command starts a background process. If true, the command will run in the background and you will not see the output. If false, the tool call will block on the command finishing, and then you will get the output. Examples of background processes: building in watch mode, starting a server. You can check the output of a background process later on by using get_terminal_output.

--- MESSAGE 22972 ---
number

--- MESSAGE 22973 ---
An optional timeout in milliseconds. When provided, the tool will stop tracking the command after this duration and return the output collected so far. Be conservative with the timeout duration, give enough time that the command would complete on a low-end machine. Use 0 for no timeout. If it's not clear how long the command will take then use 0 to avoid prematurely terminating it, never guess too low.

runSubagent

--- MESSAGE 22980 ---
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously. This tool is good at researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries, use this agent to perform the search for you.

- Agents do not run async or in the background, you will wait for the agent's result.
- When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.
- Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report. Therefore, your prompt should contain a highly detailed task description for the agent to perform autonomously and you should specify exactly what information the agent should return back to you in its final and only message to you.
- The agent's outputs should generally be trusted
- Clearly tell the agent whether you expect it to write code or just to do research (search, file reads, web fetches, etc.), since it is not aware of the user's intent
- If the user asks for a certain agent, you MUST provide that EXACT agent name (case-sensitive) to invoke that specific agent.

context7_resolve-library-id

--- MESSAGE 23036 ---
Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns a list of matching libraries.

You MUST call this function before 'context7_get-library-docs' to obtain a valid Context7-compatible library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Selection Process:
1. Analyze the query to understand what library/package the user is looking for
2. Return the most relevant match based on:
- Name similarity to the query (exact matches prioritized)
- Description relevance to the query's intent
- Documentation coverage (prioritize libraries with higher Code Snippet counts)
- Trust score (consider libraries with scores of 7-10 more authoritative)

Response Format:
- Return the selected library ID in a clearly marked section
- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen
- If multiple good matches exist, acknowledge this but proceed with the most relevant one
- If no good matches exist, clearly state this and suggest query refinements

For ambiguous queries, request clarification before proceeding with a best-guess match.. Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns a list of matching libraries.

Selection Process:

activate_github_sub_issue_management

--- MESSAGE 23092 ---
Call this tool when you need access to a new category of tools. The category of tools is described as follows:

This group of tools is designed for managing sub-issues within a parent issue in GitHub repositories. Both tools, 'mcp_github_sub_issue_write' and 'mcp_github2_sub_issue_write', serve the same purpose of adding sub-issues, allowing users to create a hierarchical structure of tasks and discussions related to a main issue. This functionality is particularly useful for teams that need to break down larger tasks into smaller, manageable components, facilitating better organization and tracking of progress. 

By using these tools, developers and project managers can enhance their workflow by ensuring that all related tasks are linked to a parent issue, making it easier to monitor dependencies and relationships between different tasks. This can lead to improved collaboration among team members, as everyone can see how their work contributes to the overall project goals. 

Additionally, the ability to add sub-issues helps in prioritizing tasks, as teams can focus on critical components of a project while keeping track of smaller, related tasks that need to be addressed. This structured approach to issue management can significantly improve project visibility and accountability. 

Overall, these tools are essential for teams utilizing GitHub for project management, as they streamline the process of issue tracking and enhance the clarity of task assignments. By integrating these tools into their workflow, teams can ensure that all aspects of their projects are well-organized and efficiently managed.

Be sure to call this tool if you need a capability related to the above.

--- MESSAGE 23094 ---
mcp_github_pull_request_review_write

--- MESSAGE 23095 ---
Create and/or submit, delete review of a pull request.

Available methods:
- create: Create a new review of a pull request. If "event" parameter is provided, the review is submitted. If "event" is omitted, a pending review is created.
- submit_pending: Submit an existing pending review of a pull request. This requires that a pending review exists for the current user on the specified pull request. The "body" and "event" parameters are used when submitting the review.
- delete_pending: Delete an existing pending review of a pull request. This requires that a pending review exists for the current user on the specified pull request.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
MOE_CYCLE PROOF-GATE - Validates mutation clusters before checkpoint
"""
import subprocess
import sys
import json
from pathlib import Path

def log(stage, status, data):
    print(json.dumps({"stage": stage, "status": status, "data": data}), flush=True)

def run_cmd(cmd, desc):
    """Run command and return success status"""
    log("PROOF_GATE", "running", {"cmd": cmd, "desc": desc})
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
    success = result.returncode == 0
    log("PROOF_GATE", "completed" if success else "failed", {
        "cmd": cmd,
        "exit_code": result.returncode,
        "stdout": result.stdout[:200],
        "stderr": result.stderr[:200]
    })
    return success

def main():
    project_root = Path(__file__).parent
    log("PROOF_GATE", "init", {"root": str(project_root)})
    
    checks = [
        ("python3 scripts/dedi_agent.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Agent syntax check"),
        ("python3 scripts/main.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Main entrypoint syntax"),
        ("python3 -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(\"docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml\"))'", "Compose YAML validity"),
        ("grep -q 'MUTATION_CLUSTER' docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml || true", "MOE cycle marker"),
    ]
    
    passed = 0
    failed = 0
    
    for cmd, desc in checks:
        if run_cmd(cmd, desc):
            passed += 1
        else:
            failed += 1
    
    log("PROOF_GATE", "summary", {"passed": passed, "failed": failed, "total": len(checks)})
    
    if failed > 0:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "REJECT", {"reason": f"{failed} checks failed"})
        sys.exit(1)
    else:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "APPROVE", {"reason": "All checks passed"})
        sys.exit(0)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

--- MESSAGE 23552 ---
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
MOE_CYCLE PROOF-GATE - Validates mutation clusters before checkpoint
"""
import subprocess
import sys
import json
from pathlib import Path

def log(stage, status, data):
    print(json.dumps({"stage": stage, "status": status, "data": data}), flush=True)

def run_cmd(cmd, desc):
    """Run command and return success status"""
    log("PROOF_GATE", "running", {"cmd": cmd, "desc": desc})
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
    success = result.returncode == 0
    log("PROOF_GATE", "completed" if success else "failed", {
        "cmd": cmd,
        "exit_code": result.returncode,
        "stdout": result.stdout[:200],
        "stderr": result.stderr[:200]
    })
    return success

def main():
    project_root = Path(__file__).parent
    log("PROOF_GATE", "init", {"root": str(project_root)})
    
    checks = [
        ("python3 scripts/dedi_agent.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Agent syntax check"),
        ("python3 scripts/main.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Main entrypoint syntax"),
        ("python3 -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(\"docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml\"))'", "Compose YAML validity"),
        ("grep -q 'MUTATION_CLUSTER' docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml || true", "MOE cycle marker"),
    ]
    
    passed = 0
    failed = 0
    
    for cmd, desc in checks:
        if run_cmd(cmd, desc):
            passed += 1
        else:
            failed += 1
    
    log("PROOF_GATE", "summary", {"passed": passed, "failed": failed, "total": len(checks)})
    
    if failed > 0:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "REJECT", {"reason": f"{failed} checks failed"})
        sys.exit(1)
    else:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "APPROVE", {"reason": "All checks passed"})
        sys.exit(0)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

--- MESSAGE 23622 ---
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
MOE_CYCLE PROOF-GATE - Validates mutation clusters before checkpoint
"""
import subprocess
import sys
import json
from pathlib import Path

def log(stage, status, data):
    print(json.dumps({"stage": stage, "status": status, "data": data}), flush=True)

def run_cmd(cmd, desc):
    """Run command and return success status"""
    log("PROOF_GATE", "running", {"cmd": cmd, "desc": desc})
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
    success = result.returncode == 0
    log("PROOF_GATE", "completed" if success else "failed", {
        "cmd": cmd,
        "exit_code": result.returncode,
        "stdout": result.stdout[:200],
        "stderr": result.stderr[:200]
    })
    return success

def main():
    project_root = Path(__file__).parent
    log("PROOF_GATE", "init", {"root": str(project_root)})
    
    checks = [
        ("python3 scripts/dedi_agent.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Agent syntax check"),
        ("python3 scripts/main.py --help 2>&1 | head -5", "Main entrypoint syntax"),
        ("python3 -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(\"docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml\"))'", "Compose YAML validity"),
        ("grep -q 'MUTATION_CLUSTER' docker-compose.chronos-v3.yml || true", "MOE cycle marker"),
    ]
    
    passed = 0
    failed = 0
    
    for cmd, desc in checks:
        if run_cmd(cmd, desc):
            passed += 1
        else:
            failed += 1
    
    log("PROOF_GATE", "summary", {"passed": passed, "failed": failed, "total": len(checks)})
    
    if failed > 0:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "REJECT", {"reason": f"{failed} checks failed"})
        sys.exit(1)
    else:
        log("PROOF_GATE", "APPROVE", {"reason": "All checks passed"})
        sys.exit(0)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

- **VS Code integration**: The wrapper now sources the VS Code shell integration script if `VSCODE_SHELL_INTEGRATION` is provided (or the default vscode-server path when `TERM_PROGRAM=vscode`). Logging notes which file was sourced.

  - Only our bash children are cleaned up; the aggressive `-9` catch-all was removed to avoid killing unrelated builds.
- Smoke tests:
  - Non-whitelisted (`sleep 6; echo …`) timed out cleanly.
  - Whitelisted (`npm run build && sleep 6`) ran through (npm complained about missing script, but the wrapper didn’t time it out).

- `AIS_SHELL_TIMEOUT_ENABLED` (true/false)
- `AIS_SHELL_TIMEOUT` (seconds)
- `AIS_SHELL_TIMEOUT_WHITELIST` (regex fragments, space-separated)

--- MESSAGE 23948 ---
apply_patch

--- MESSAGE 23949 ---
Use the `apply_patch` tool to edit files.
Your patch language is a stripped-down, file-oriented diff format designed to be easy to parse and safe to apply. You can think of it as a high-level envelope:

*** Begin Patch
[ one or more file sections ]
*** End Patch

Within that envelope, you get a sequence of file operations.
You MUST include a header to specify the action you are taking.
Each operation starts with one of three headers:

*** Add File: <path> - create a new file. Every following line is a + line (the initial contents).
*** Delete File: <path> - remove an existing file. Nothing follows.
*** Update File: <path> - patch an existing file in place (optionally with a rename).

May be immediately followed by *** Move to: <new path> if you want to rename the file.
Then one or more “hunks”, each introduced by @@ (optionally followed by a hunk header).
Within a hunk each line starts with:

For instructions on [context_before] and [context_after]:
- By default, show 3 lines of code immediately above and 3 lines immediately below each change. If a change is within 3 lines of a previous change, do NOT duplicate the first change's [context_after] lines in the second change's [context_before] lines.
- If 3 lines of context is insufficient to uniquely identify the snippet of code within the file, use the @@ operator to indicate the class or function to which the snippet belongs. For instance, we might have:
@@ class BaseClass
[3 lines of pre-context]
- [old_code]
+ [new_code]
[3 lines of post-context]

- If a code block is repeated so many times in a class or function such that even a single `@@` statement and 3 lines of context cannot uniquely identify the snippet of code, you can use multiple `@@` statements to jump to the right context. For instance:

@@ class BaseClass
@@ 	 def method():
[3 lines of pre-context]
- [old_code]
+ [new_code]
[3 lines of post-context]

The full grammar definition is below:
Patch := Begin { FileOp } End
Begin := "*** Begin Patch" NEWLINE
End := "*** End Patch" NEWLINE
FileOp := AddFile | DeleteFile | UpdateFile
AddFile := "*** Add File: " path NEWLINE { "+" line NEWLINE }
DeleteFile := "*** Delete File: " path NEWLINE
UpdateFile := "*** Update File: " path NEWLINE [ MoveTo ] { Hunk }
MoveTo := "*** Move to: " newPath NEWLINE
Hunk := "@@" [ header ] NEWLINE { HunkLine } [ "*** End of File" NEWLINE ]
HunkLine := (" " | "-" | "+") text NEWLINE

A full patch can combine several operations:

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: hello.txt
+Hello world
*** Update File: src/app.py
*** Move to: src/main.py
@@ def greet():
-print("Hi")
+print("Hello, world!")
*** Delete File: obsolete.txt
*** End Patch

It is important to remember:

- You must include a header with your intended action (Add/Delete/Update)
- You must prefix new lines with `+` even when creating a new file
- File references must be ABSOLUTE, NEVER RELATIVE.

Search for files in the workspace by glob pattern. This only returns the paths of matching files. Use this tool when you know the exact filename pattern of the files you're searching for. Glob patterns match from the root of the workspace folder. Examples:
- **/*.{js,ts} to match all js/ts files in the workspace.
- src/** to match all files under the top-level src folder.
- **/foo/**/*.js to match all js files under any foo folder in the workspace.

grep_search

--- MESSAGE 23985 ---
Do a fast text search in the workspace. Use this tool when you want to search with an exact string or regex. If you are not sure what words will appear in the workspace, prefer using regex patterns with alternation (|) or character classes to search for multiple potential words at once instead of making separate searches. For example, use 'function|method|procedure' to look for all of those words at once. Use includePattern to search within files matching a specific pattern, or in a specific file, using a relative path. Use 'includeIgnoredFiles' to include files normally ignored by .gitignore, other ignore files, and `files.exclude` and `search.exclude` settings. Warning: using this may cause the search to be slower, only set it when you want to search in ignored folders like node_modules or build outputs. Use this tool when you want to see an overview of a particular file, instead of using read_file many times to look for code within a file.
